New: BloomBar Café et Fleurs plans its first Manhattan shop on the Upper East Side

1 week ago
Team YeahThatsKosher
1 week ago
Add Comment
3 Min Read
    Share This!
    FacebookXEmailLinkedInRedditWhatsApp
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:47
Instaread

BloomBar Café et Fleurs plans to open its first Manhattan shop on the Upper East Side in late October 2026. The café and flower shop already has locations in New Jersey and Brooklyn.

A café with a flower shop

Customers can stop for coffee or browse gifts and home décor. BloomBar also sells clean beauty products and flowers to take home. The company describes its changing menu as organic and clean.

The business began during COVID as a small flower market in a New Jersey enclave. A café followed.

Matcha, cold brew and soft serve

BloomBar started serving matcha four years ago and imports it directly from Japan. Its lattes use plant and oat milks batched in house.

As Clean Coffee’s exclusive café partner, BloomBar serves its single-origin organic cold brew. It also makes vegan soft serve with a fava bean base. The soft serve is non-dairy and gluten free. Salads and fresh pastries from local bakers are available too.

Flower arrangements and gifts

The flower market makes signature bouquets and vase arrangements for pickup or delivery. The shops also carry gifts and home décor, with clean beauty products and flowers available to grab and go.

The founders

Heleyne and Ronnie Tamir previously owned Cantaloup, a fashion chain on the Upper East Side, in the early 2000s. Before founding BloomBar, Heleyne spent 15 years in luxury beauty and co-founded Surratt Beauty.

“BloomBar is where people come for life’s small moments, like coffee with a friend or an hour to themselves,” Heleyne Tamir said. “We want those moments to happen surrounded by beauty, in a space that feels transporting yet completely at ease.”

BloomBar locations

The Upper East Side shop is set to be the company’s eighth location, counting its vegan soft serve concept, Ripe. A ninth location is planned for Monmouth Square in Eatontown, NJ, in spring 2027.

Upper East Side plans and existing locations’ kosher certification

The new BloomBar Café et Fleurs is at 1226 Third Avenue at East 71st Street, New York, NY, with an opening planned for late October 2026.

BloomBar’s existing locations in Long Branch, Allenhurst and Deal, NJ, and its Brooklyn shops at 1013 Avenue K and 511 Avenue U are certified by Vaad Kashrus Mehadrin. These locations are Cholov Stam and Pas Yisroel.

NEW: PopUp Bagels Opens Kosher Spot in Tenafly, NJ

1 week ago
Team YeahThatsKosher
1 week ago
Add Comment
2 Min Read
    Share This!
    FacebookXEmailLinkedInRedditWhatsApp

PopUp Bagels, the hot-bagel chain behind the “Grip, Rip and Dip” craze, opens its first Bergen County shop this Friday, October 9, in Tenafly, New Jersey, and the new location is kosher certified. It is the chain’s second New Jersey store, following its July debut in Westfield.

The Tenafly Grand Opening

The grand opening celebration runs from 7:00 to 11:00 AM on Friday with hot bagels, iced tea from Saint James Iced Tea, and a limited-edition Capon’s Carrot Cake Schmear created with chef Josh Capon of Capon’s Chophouse in Hackensack. The Tenafly-exclusive schmear is available while supplies last. PopUp Bagels previously ran pop-ups in Tenafly and Midland Park before signing a lease for a permanent shop on Washington Street, and plans at least two dozen New Jersey locations.

The PopUp Bagels Concept

PopUp Bagels is not a typical bagel store. There is no slicing, no toasting and no breakfast sandwiches. Bagels come out of the oven hot, are sold whole by the bag, and are meant to be torn apart and dipped into whipped schmears. The lineup is plain, salt, sesame, poppy seed and everything.

Founder Adam Goldberg, a New Jersey native who grew up in Livingston and Short Hills, launched the brand as a pandemic-era pop-up out of a backyard window in Connecticut. It has since grown to more than 50 locations nationwide. The Tenafly shop is run by franchisee Just Pop.

PopUp Bagels Tenafly Info & Kosher Certification

PopUp Bagels is located at 6-8 Washington Street in downtown Tenafly, NJ 07670, in Bergen County near the Jewish communities of Englewood and Teaneck. Hours are Monday through Sunday, 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM.

The Tenafly shop is kosher certified under National Kosher Supervision (NKS), led by Rabbi Aaron Mehlman, the same supervision as the chain’s New York locations. The certification covers the bagels (pareve, non-Pas Yisroel) and the plain and scallion cream cheeses (dairy, non cholov yisroel). The rotating flavored schmears are not certified.

Other Kosher PopUp Bagels Locations

These are other PopUp Bagels locations YeahThatsKosher has reported as kosher certified, each linked to our coverage at the time.
